messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNullRecordSeparatorCsv106` creates a CSVFormat with a semicolon delimiter, skipping the header record and setting a header. It then formats two values "A" and "B" using `CSVFormat.format(Object...)` and asserts the result does not end with "null". The complaint is the output is "A;Bnull" instead of "A;B".

Looking at the format method, it uses a StringWriter and a CSVPrinter to print the record and then returns the output trimmed. The CSVPrinter's printRecord method prints each value and then calls println. The println method appends the recordSeparator string from the CSVFormat to the output.

The CSVFormat's recordSeparator field is set from the constructor, and newFormat(char) creates a CSVFormat with null as the recordSeparator. This explains why "null" (the string) is appended during println: the recordSeparator string is null, so appending it appends literal "null". The constructor stores this directly without null-safety or default value assignment for recordSeparator.

Therefore, the root cause is that when recordSeparator is not set (i.e., null), the println method appends the literal "null" string because it blindly appends the recordSeparator string, which is null, resulting in the undesired output.

The fix should address how recordSeparator null values are handled, likely by defaulting recordSeparator to a line break or an empty string instead of null, or by checking in CSVPrinter.println() for null before appending.

Recent bug reports have no relevance to this issue since they concern record-to-map conversion, unrelated to CSV formatting or record separator usage.

Hence, the bug arises because CSVFormat allows null recordSeparator which causes literal "null" to be appended by CSVPrinter.println().

Which methods to fix:
- org.apache.commons.csv.CSVFormat.CSVFormat(char, Character, QuoteMode, Character, Character, boolean, boolean, String, String, String[], boolean)
- org.apache.commons.csv.CSVPrinter.println()

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
